title: Buy Two Chocolates
summary: Given an integer array prices representing the prices of chocolates and an integer money, select exactly two chocolates such that the leftover money is non-negative and as small as possible.
statement: Given an integer array prices representing the prices of chocolates and an integer money, select exactly two chocolates such that the leftover money is non-negative and as small as possible. If buying two chocolates results in a negative amount of money, return the initial amount of money.
constraints: Identify the two distinct chocolates with the lowest prices.
Buy both when their combined cost does not exceed money.
Return the remaining money after that purchase, or the original money when those two are unaffordable.
hints: If their sum exceeds money, every other pair also exceeds money.
Otherwise subtract exactly that sum from the available money.
The two order statistics uniquely determine the requested cheapest pair, and the affordability check handles both possible outcomes.
editorial: The two order statistics uniquely determine the requested cheapest pair, and the affordability check handles both possible outcomes.

tests.explanation: Buying prices one and two spends all three dollars, leaving zero.
The two cheapest chocolates cost five, so no pair is affordable and all three dollars remain.
